column1: # MODE: PROD
# Which artifacts belong to which integration mode.
# A skill that offers more than one way to be driven declares it here, and
# `install.sh --integration <skill>=<mode>` picks one without a prompt, so an
# agent can choose its own interface headlessly.
# The rule is deliberately narrow: a binary named below installs ONLY in its
# mode, and every file not named installs in every mode. So SKILL.md, the
# docs and the two prebuilt binaries below are never mode-dependent, and a
# skill with no integration.tsv at all has one mode and is unaffected by the
# flag.
# `skill` is the default, because it is the interface that needs no client
# configuration and no running server -- an agent drives the two binaries
# below directly, exactly as SKILL.md/docs/README.md describe. `mcp` is
# opt-in: its tools are listed in every session that configures the server,
# so it is worth choosing rather than assuming.
# interactive-shell itself is deliberately UNLISTED, not `skill`-only: BOTH
# modes need it. In skill mode it is the PTY wrapper an agent starts
# directly; in mcp mode interactive-shell-mcp's own `start` tool spawns it
# as a child (resolved as a sibling of its own binary, mirroring
# ai-text-editor-mcp's server autostart) -- listing it as `skill`-only would
# ship an mcp-only install whose `start` tool could never actually launch a
# session.
mode
skill
column3: CLI input client the skill's own instructions drive directly
